items.title: Effect of Different Ligands on ΔE and Colour

source_refs.note: Effect of Different Ligands on ΔE and Colour: a main subheading of 18.6.1 Colour Formation, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 27-27.

blocks.text: The nature of the ligand affects the magnitude of the splitting, ΔE. Some ligands like NH₃, CN⁻ cause larger splitting, increasing the energy gap (ΔE). Whereas, for some other ligands like Cl⁻, I⁻, ΔE is smaller. A larger ΔE means a higher frequency, (shorter wavelength) of light must be absorbed that is in the region of violet or blue colour. Corresponding to that a yellow light is reflected giving the compound a yellow colour. Some complexes absorb low-energy light (red/orange) and appear blue or green according to the complementary colour scheme. Ligands can be arranged in order of their ability to cause d-orbital splitting (from high ΔE to low ΔE):

blocks.text_alt: CN⁻ > en > NH₃ > H₂O > OH⁻ > Cl⁻ > Br⁻ > I⁻

blocks.prompt: a) How does the presence of ligands affect the degeneracy of d-orbitals in a complex ion?
blocks.explanation: The electric field of the ligands splits the five degenerate d orbitals into two non-degenerate sets of different energy.

blocks.prompt: b) Describe the key difference in d-orbital splitting patterns between octahedral complexes and tetrahedral complexes.
blocks.explanation: In both, the five d orbitals split into two sets, but the order is reversed:

blocks.prompt: c) Explain the relationship between the absorbed light energy (ΔE) and the observed colour of a transition metal complex. Reference Planck's equation (ΔE=hν=hc/λ).
blocks.explanation: A larger ΔE means light of higher frequency and shorter wavelength is absorbed; the colour we see is the complementary colour of the light absorbed.

blocks.prompt: d) If a complex containing the ligand Cl⁻ absorbs light in the red/orange region of the spectrum, what general colour range would you expect the complex to appear?
blocks.explanation: Blue to green, the complementary colours of orange and red.

blocks.prompt: e) Explain the phenomenon (d-d transitions) responsible for the colour of transition metal compounds.
blocks.explanation: In the split d orbitals an electron in the lower set absorbs a photon whose energy equals ΔE and moves to the upper set. That colour is removed from white light, and the remaining colours are seen.
